{{Short description|Concept in computability theory}}
In [[computability theory]], a set <math>P</math> of functions <math>\mathbb{N} \rarr \mathbb{N}</math> is said to be '''Mučnik-reducible''' to another set <math>Q</math> of functions <math>\mathbb{N} \rarr \mathbb{N}</math> when for every function <math>g</math> in <math>Q</math>, there exists a function <math>f</math> in <math>P</math> that is [[Turing-reducible]] to <math>g</math>.{{r|hinman}}

Unlike most [[reduction (computability theory)|reducibility relations]] in computability, Mučnik reducibility is not defined between functions <math>\mathbb{N} \rarr \mathbb{N}</math> but between sets of such functions. These sets are called "mass problems" and can be viewed as problems with more than one solution. Informally, <math>P</math> is Mučnik-reducible to <math>Q</math> when any solution of <math>Q</math> can be used to compute some solution of <math>P</math>.{{r|simpson}}
